inquiry.title: The maintained candle flame
inquiry.question: What stabilizes the visible flame while its material inventory is continuously replaced?

observation.statement: A candle flame retains a recognizable position and form while wax vapor, oxygen, products, and heat continuously cross its boundary.
observation.instrument: vision; optional thermocouple, balance, and gas analyzer
observation.location: still indoor air at standard room conditions
observation.uncertainty: air motion, wick geometry, wax composition, and measurement disturbance alter the envelope
observation.reproduction: repeat with the same candle and controlled airflow

reference.local_zero: the same candle and room conditions before ignition, with no sustained flame envelope
reference.justification: the comparison isolates the maintained combustion departure without treating the local unlit state as the origin of all scale

departure.description: a luminous, heat-releasing, non-equilibrium steady-state reaction envelope
departure.magnitude: measured by luminosity, temperature field, and reaction rate
departure.duration: while fuel, oxidizer, ignition temperature, and pressure remain admissible

active_enclosure.name: visible combustion envelope
active_enclosure.boundary: the spatial region in which reaction, luminosity, and temperature remain above the declared detection thresholds
active_enclosure.maintained_identity: a flame of stable mean location and recognizable geometry
required_conditions: pressure and flow within a stable regime

enclosing_enclosures.name: room atmosphere
enclosing_enclosures.boundary: the pressure and composition field surrounding the flame
enclosing_enclosures.maintained_identity: an oxygen-bearing atmosphere near room pressure
enclosing_enclosures.projection_carrier: molecular collision, diffusion, convection, and pressure
enclosing_enclosures.variation_test: reduce oxygen concentration or impose airflow while holding candle geometry approximately fixed and measure the change in flame persistence

enclosed_enclosures.name: wick and vaporization interface
enclosed_enclosures.boundary: wick surface and adjacent wax-vapor region
enclosed_enclosures.maintained_identity: capillary fuel delivery and vapor formation
enclosed_enclosures.contribution: delivers wax vapor and heat-coupled fuel flow into the reaction envelope

parallel_enclosures.name: buoyant exhaust plume
parallel_enclosures.boundary: rising region of heated products above the flame
parallel_enclosures.maintained_identity: a convective plume carrying products and heat away

exchanges.uncertainty: requires synchronized mass and exhaust measurements

exchanges.boundary: atmosphere to flame and flame to room
exchanges.stored: transient thermal energy in wax, wick, gases, and nearby surfaces
exchanges.transformed: radiation, convection, conduction, and chemical products
exchanges.uncertainty: open-room calorimetry does not capture every path

ivm_passage.vector_equilibrium: the stable mean flame geometry under the declared fuel, oxygen, pressure, and flow conditions
ivm_passage.periphery_boundary: the reaction envelope at which heat release and reactant supply no longer sustain the declared flame geometry
ivm_passage.saturation_quantity: departure of oxygen supply, heat release, and flow from the stable mean flame condition
ivm_passage.capacity_condition: the current macroscopic combustion enclosure ceases to maintain a stable visible flame when projected atmospheric conditions cross the sustaining range
preserved_across_passage: energy transformed into heat, radiation, and stored thermal states
ivm_passage.post_passage_projection: the room atmosphere continues to project pressure, composition, and heat-removal conditions into the transformed state

escalation.trigger: room-scale ventilation or pressure dominates flame-local conditions
escalation.destination: room atmosphere and building airflow enclosure

deescalation.trigger: macroscopic averages fail to account for reaction or transport

final_frontier.observed_end: the instrumented room, candle, flame envelope, and measured exhaust during the burn interval
final_frontier.derived_end: mass and energy pathways supported by the selected thermodynamic, fluid, and reaction models
final_frontier.unavailable: unmeasured microscopic trajectories and influences beyond the instrumented room and time interval
final_frontier.halt_reason: the inquiry ends where available instruments and the declared model cannot distinguish further boundary contributions
prohibited_promotions: a bounded residual is not proof of destruction
the room boundary is not the end of physical scale
a stable flame shape is not a static material inventory

target.boundary_condition: oxygen partial pressure projected by the enclosing atmosphere
target.intervention: vary oxygen concentration in a controlled chamber while holding wick, wax, pressure, and airflow within measured bounds
target.prediction: below a reproducible oxygen condition the enclosing atmosphere will no longer sustain the flame departure and the visible envelope will collapse
target.alternative: if flame persistence is unchanged across the admissible oxygen variation, the proposed active projection is incomplete or incorrectly targeted
target.falsification: the flame remains stable after the mapped projected condition is removed while all replacement conditions and exchanges are measured
return_path: compare with the declared local zero
revise the active enclosure or reject the proposed projection

unresolved: complete calorimetric closure is not supplied by this example
the scale-transition thresholds are operational choices, not universal constants
